input.sql: SELECT service_type, is_scheduled, class, SUM(passengers) AS passengers, SUM(passengers) FILTER (WHERE distance >= 3000) AS pax_ge_3000, SUM(passengers) FILTER (WHERE distance >= 2000) AS pax_ge_2000, SUM(passengers) FILTER (WHERE distance >= 3500) AS pax_ge_3500, SUM(departures_performed) AS departures, SUM(departures_performed) FILTER (WHERE distance >= 3000) AS dep_ge_3000 FROM v_t100_segment WHERE origin_airport_id = 10299 AND period_month >= DATE '2025-08-01' AND period_month <= DATE '2026-07-01' GROUP BY service_type, is_scheduled, class ORDER BY passengers DESC

answer.headline: Passenger long-haul share at ANC is {F1} ({F1.period})
answer.body:
Over {F1.period}, the calculated share of passenger traffic departing Ted Stevens Anchorage International (ANC) on long-haul segments is {F1}. The definition is {F1.definition}. Observed passenger-scope enplanements in that window are {F7}, and observed seats offered on that same passenger scope are {F9}. The catalog cannot weight long-haul share by seats, so {F9} describes capacity offered, not a second proportion.

Scheduled service is not a filter on the catalog metric. An exploratory cut to BTS class F on passenger aircraft gives the ratio {F63}, long-haul passengers {F11} divided by scheduled passenger enplanements {F10}. The renderer shows that exploratory result as a ratio, on the same zero-to-one scale as the catalog share, which is shown as a percent. That scheduled slice is {F67} of observed passenger-scope enplanements {F7}. Scheduled combi passengers are {F24}, and that row returned no long-haul passenger total. Class G passenger-aircraft passengers are {F50}.

The proportion moves sharply with the distance cutoff. The calculated passenger-scope share is {F3} under {F3.definition} and {F4} under {F4.definition}. The exploratory scheduled-class ratios at those cutoffs are {F64} and {F65}.

A share of flights is a different quantity. The calculated passenger-scope departure share is {F2}, using {F2.definition}. The exploratory share among scheduled class F passenger departures is {F66}, from {F15} of {F14}.

Cargo is not part of the passenger result. At the catalog default cutoff, the calculated long-haul share of freight tonnage is {F60} and of freight departures is {F61}. Across all configurations the departure share is {F62}.

claims.text: Over {F1.period}, the calculated long-haul share of departing passenger traffic at ANC is {F1}, defined as {F1.definition}. Observed passenger-scope enplanements are {F7} and observed seats offered are {F9}.
Restricting to BTS scheduled class F on passenger aircraft, the exploratory long-haul passenger ratio is {F63}, from {F11} over {F10}. That scheduled slice is {F67} of passenger-scope enplanements.
At the other catalog cutoffs, the calculated passenger-scope shares are {F3} ({F3.definition}) and {F4} ({F4.definition}). The exploratory scheduled-class ratios are {F64} and {F65}.
Weighted by departures, the calculated passenger-scope long-haul share is {F2}. The exploratory scheduled class F passenger departure share is {F66}, from {F15} over {F14}.

Freight and all-configuration shares at the catalog default cutoff are {F60} for freight tonnage, {F61} for freight departures, and {F62} for all departures. These are not the passenger-traffic proportion.

For passenger traffic in this window, the catalog share {F1} is a close reading of scheduled class F traffic because that class is {F67} of passenger-scope enplanements and the exploratory scheduled ratio is {F63}. The departure-weighted shares {F2} and {F66} answer a different question and are lower.

assumptions: ANC is Ted Stevens Anchorage International Airport. Merrill Field is a separate Anchorage airport and is excluded.
The question names no period, so every catalog figure uses the trailing T12 of departing T-100 segments, {F1.period}.
Long-haul means the catalog default in {F1.definition}. The question does not set a distance cutoff, so the other catalog cutoffs are reported beside it.
Passenger traffic means enplaned passengers, so the primary weight is passengers. Departure-weighted figures are a separate reading of the share of flights.

Scheduled is not a catalog parameter. The exploratory cut keeps BTS service class F on passenger-configured aircraft. The catalog passenger scope also includes non-scheduled service plus combi and seaplane configurations.
Out of means segments departing ANC, not arrivals.
limitations: Figures are performed segment enplanements, including connections, not a forward published schedule and not origin-destination journeys. A long segment is not the same thing as a long passenger itinerary.
Scheduled combi passengers are {F24}, with no long-haul passenger total returned for that row. Class G passenger-aircraft passengers are {F50}.
Exploratory ratios are not catalog metrics.
Cargo long-haul shares {F60} and {F61}, and the all-configuration departure share {F62}, describe a different operation and are not the passenger result.
The cutoff is a parameter. {F3} and {F4} show that another catalog cutoff changes the passenger proportion by a wide margin.
Unmet demand, terminal capacity, fares, and profitability are not measured by this data.
